events.title: The election of Pope Urban VII
events.shortBlurb: Giovanni Battista Castagna was chosen pope as Urban VII and was dead of malaria before his coronation — the shortest pontificate on record…
body: Sixtus V died on 27 August 1590, and on 15 September the cardinals, swayed by the Spanish faction, elected Giovanni Battista Castagna, who took the name Urban VII. He was a Roman of a Genoese house, sixty-nine years old, a doctor of laws of Bologna who had served the Curia as Referendary of the Signatura, archbishop of Rossano, and Inquisitor General of the Roman Inquisition, and he had been cardinal these seven years.

He was already sick when elected. The malaria of the Roman summer was on him, and on 27 September, twelve days after his election and before he could be crowned, he died toward midnight. His is the shortest pontificate the Church remembers.

He was buried in St. Peter's, whence his remains were later carried to Santa Maria sopra Minerva. The cardinals returned to the Sistine Chapel and in December chose Gregory XIV; the year had seen three men bear the name of pope.
